adminDecisions.question: When a quotation passes its validity date, should it expire on a timer into a state of its own, or simply be reported as lapsed while staying `sent`?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option A: quotation expiry becomes a canonical business state. sent -> lapsed, represented in the persisted quotation state rather than calculated at render or query time. Owner's rationale: a quotation past its validity is not equivalent to an active sent quotation, and keeping it 'sent' forces every consumer, agent, report and automation to calculate expiry independently, risking inconsistent business behaviour. ELEVEN REQUIREMENTS recorded as given: add lapsed using the existing state architecture; add the sent -> lapsed transition; implement expiry on the existing job/event infrastructure; make it idempotent; preserve the original quotation, version and history; keep the existing acceptance-after-expiry rejection enforced; review every consumer of sent; do not invent behaviour for payment, project creation, notifications, renewal/versioning or client messaging; raise a decision rather than invent one; add unit, integration, transition, scheduler, idempotency and regression tests; do not mark G-111 complete until fully verified. CONSUMER REVIEW PERFORMED 2026-08-14 under requirement 7, before any implementation. Six consumers of 'sent' found. Three raise no question: send_proposal (approved -> sent) is unaffected; payment is tied to an accepted quote and a lapsed quote is not accepted; project creation likewise, and is separately ADM-72. One is derivable and is recorded on G-111 rather than raised: the proposals_live_version_key index defines live as 'still on its way to an answer', which a lapsed quote is not, so lapsed leaves the live set and frees the deal for a new quotation. Three require decisions and are raised as ADM-77, ADM-78 and ADM-79.

adminDecisions.question: Should an accepted quotation become a fourth condition on projects.start_project, alongside the verified advance, an approved requirement version and the WhatsApp group?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option B: an Admin may create a project without an accepted quotation. An accepted quotation is NOT a universal hard prerequisite for project creation. Recorded as given: the system must preserve whether a project has an accepted quotation; projects.proposal_id may remain nullable; do not fabricate a quotation or acceptance; do not auto-create a fake proposal to satisfy the workflow; the absence must remain visible and auditable; client-funded workflows still enforce the payment and start conditions ADM-13 already defines; do NOT add accepted quotation as a fourth ADM-13 start condition; do NOT change ADM-13; do NOT make quotation requirements project-type-specific, which option B makes unnecessary. HISTORICAL DATA: existing projects with no quotation are valid under this decision, and no fake quotation or acceptance record is to be backfilled. IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW 2026-08-14, performed before writing anything. Eight of the nine requirements are already satisfied and need no code: proposal_id exists and is nullable with a partial index on the non-null case; convertToProject carries the link when it exists and never demands it; nothing anywhere fabricates a proposal; start_project still enforces exactly ADM-13's three conditions; and no project-type vocabulary is involved. AUDITABILITY VERIFIED, not assumed: projects.projects carries the audit_row_change trigger from G-093/ADM-51, and the vocabulary gives INSERT 'project.created' with a 'project.updated' fallback, so both creating a project without a quotation and linking one later are recorded in audit.audit_log. ONE REQUIREMENT IS NOT MET: 'visible'. Nothing reads projects.proposal_id for display - createProject writes it and no page, panel or report shows whether a project has an accepted quotation. The absence is auditable but not visible. Identified as an implementation task on G-114 rather than built; the gate bars it.

adminDecisions.question: Which project types does the agency actually distinguish, so the onboarding checklist can be configurable by type as Document 10 §6 asks?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED. The agency provides all types of application and web development services, so AgencyOS must NOT restrict projects to a small hardcoded list of service categories. Web Development, Mobile App, E-commerce, SaaS, AI, UI/UX are examples of services, technologies and use cases - not exclusive project types. The stated business principle: AgencyOS should model WHAT THE CLIENT PROJECT IS and WHAT HAS BEEN SOLD, rather than artificially limiting what the agency is capable of selling. One project may contain a web application, a mobile application, an admin panel, an API, UI/UX, AI integration, third-party integrations, deployment and maintenance, and must be representable without a new project type. TEN REQUIREMENTS recorded as given: any type of web or application work; scope and requirements define the actual services and features; technologies coexist within one project; new service categories must not require a migration; the system must not assume every project follows the same onboarding checklist; the 17-item checklist remains the baseline; items may be not_applicable where appropriate; any retained templates must be Admin-configurable rather than hardcoded; do not invent project types from the repository; do not populate an empty project-type or template table with fake data. INSPECTION PERFORMED 2026-08-14, as the decision required, before proposing anything. NO project_type FIELD EXISTS ANYWHERE - not in any migration, not in src, not in app. So requirements 1 through 4 are already satisfied by construction rather than by work: nothing restricts a project to a category, and no migration is needed when the agency sells something new. What the project IS is already modelled by projects.modules -> projects.features -> tasks, with provenance back to crm.requirement_versions via G-020's break_down_requirement. What was SOLD is already modelled by sales.proposal_items, each a described priced line. A web application plus a mobile application plus an admin panel plus an AI integration is four modules on one project today, and needs nothing new. CONCLUSION on the implementation question the owner posed: a separate project_type field is NOT necessary for classification, and adding an enum would be exactly the rigidity this decision forbids.

adminDecisions.question: How should a WhatsApp reply become an authenticated approval decision? decide_approval requires a signed-in approver by design (directive §29); a sender is an unverified phone number, and core.users has no phone. Options: a verified phone-to-user link with a service-role path to decide on behalf of an identified human, or replies stay advisory and settling stays in the approvals UI.
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option A: a WhatsApp reply is ADVISORY ONLY. The actual approval must be performed through the authenticated AgencyOS UI. Owner's reason: AgencyOS already requires an authenticated approver for consequential decisions, and a message reading 'Approved' must not become binding merely because it came from a phone number associated with a contact, staff member or group participant. The WhatsApp channel MAY deliver the request, provide the reference, notify the approver and direct the approver to AgencyOS. The reply itself MUST NOT settle the approval. The authoritative path remains: authenticated AgencyOS user -> approval request -> required-role verification -> money-floor policy -> approval decision -> audit trail. TEN REQUIREMENTS, recorded as given: (1) do NOT add core.users.phone merely to support WhatsApp approval; (2) do NOT implement phone-number matching for approval authorization; (3) do NOT create a new WhatsApp-based approval identity system; (4) do NOT create a signed approval link unless separately requested; (5) do NOT change the approval engine's authenticated-user requirement; (6) preserve the existing approval reference mechanism; (7) WhatsApp messages remain advisory/notification events; (8) the approval engine remains the only authoritative mechanism for consequential approval; (9) agents must never be able to bypass the authenticated approval boundary; (10) do not mark G-110 production-complete. CONSEQUENCE FOUND WHILE RECORDING, NOT IMPLEMENTED: the announcement built by announcementFor() in src/modules/crm/schema.ts ends with the line 'Reply quoting <reference>.' - it instructs the approver to reply in WhatsApp. Under this decision nothing reads that reply and nothing ever will, so an approver who follows the instruction believes they have approved something they have not. The wording must direct the approver to AgencyOS instead. Recorded as remaining scope on G-110 and deliberately NOT changed: the decision gate bars product changes.

adminDecisions.question: Should a group message be attributed to a crm.contacts row by phone match, or does attribution need the same verified phone-to-identity link ADM-74 asks for? A wrong match puts words in a named client's mouth in a transcript they can see.
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option C: no individual attribution. AgencyOS must NOT infer or assert the identity of a group-message sender from a phone-number match alone. Recorded as given: preserve the provider-supplied sender number in message metadata where available; keep author_id null unless a separately verified identity mechanism exists; do not map the sender to crm.contacts merely because the phone matches; do not claim a contact personally authored the message; do not add core.users.phone for this purpose; do not create a phone-based identity system; do not introduce a new verification mechanism. The transcript must remain honest about what AgencyOS actually knows. SCOPE: this is the decision for the CURRENT system. It is NOT a statement that provider-level sender attribution is impossible, and it may be revisited after real provider verification establishes what identity information the provider actually supplies. IMPLEMENTATION CHECK 2026-08-14: the existing implementation already satisfies option C point for point, so NO CODE IS REQUIRED. crm.ingest_group_message writes author_id as a literal null, keeps the normalised sender number on message metadata, and maps nothing to crm.contacts; tests/group-ingest.test.ts pins the null. Per the owner's instruction, no unnecessary code was created.

adminDecisions.question: Should leads converted before G-086 have their qualification date backfilled, and with what date? The conversion date is the only defensible candidate and is still a guess; the alternative is a visible hole in historic funnel reports.
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option C: historical qualified_at values remain NULL. Do NOT backfill from converted_at. Owner's rationale: qualified_at and converted_at represent different business events, and if AgencyOS did not record the actual qualification event for a historical lead, a qualification timestamp must not be manufactured from another event merely because it is available. EIGHT REQUIREMENTS recorded as given: historical NULLs remain NULL; converted_at is not a substitute; no inferred timestamp; no inferred_at or inferred flag column added merely to make a backfill possible; G-086's forward behaviour unchanged; the historical constraint is not to be validated by fabricating data; historical funnel reports must tolerate NULL qualified_at; and if a future report needs to distinguish recorded history from missing history it must surface the NULL honestly rather than silently filling it. VERIFICATION PERFORMED 2026-08-14 before closing anything, as the decision required. Every reader of qualified_at in the repository was enumerated. Exactly one writes it - src/modules/crm/service.ts:576, on the move into 'qualified', which is G-086's forward behaviour and is unchanged. src/lib/db/types.ts already types it 'string | null' in all three shapes, so the application tolerates the NULL today. The remaining references are verify scripts asserting the behaviour. THERE ARE NO FUNNEL REPORTS AT ALL, so requirement 7 constrains future work rather than demanding present work, and requirement 8 is conditional on a report that does not exist. Requirements 1-6 are satisfied by doing nothing, which is what option C asks for. REQUIREMENTS 7 AND 8 ARE STANDING: any future reporting work inherits them, and a report that fills a NULL rather than showing it would violate this decision.

adminDecisions.question: Which situations trigger automated follow-up and what timing should be used?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, with the attempt-limit correction of the same day. Follow-up is defined as reusable RHYTHMS that situations point at, rather than a separate cadence per situation. SITUATIONS. (1) No response after quotation - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply, accept/reject, quote expiry or deal close, escalates to Sales Agent or Owner. (2) No response after requirements request - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply or requirements received, escalates to Sales Agent. (3) No response after proposal - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply, accept/reject or deal close, escalates to Sales Agent or Owner. (4) Abandoned conversation - Sales-Nurture, automated YES, stops on reply, lead closed/lost or explicit opt-out, escalates to Sales Agent. (5) Pending approval - Internal-Approval, automated YES, stops on approved/rejected/cancelled, escalates required approver then Owner; INTERNAL communication, explicitly NOT governed by the client/lead consent gate. (6) Pending payment - Payment-Followup, automated DEFERRED, stops on payment verified, invoice cancelled/refunded or explicit close, escalates to Finance or Owner. (7) Inactive lead - Sales-Nurture, automated YES, stops on reply, lead converted/lost/closed or opt-out, escalates to Sales Agent. (8) Post-project - Customer-Success, automated YES, stops on response, completed follow-up or opt-out, escalates to Customer Success. RHYTHMS, with Day 0 the trigger and NOT an attempt, and every day number a BUSINESS day. Sales-Active: first at day 2, maximum 7 attempts, spacing 3, sends on days 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Sales-Nurture: first at day 7, maximum 7, spacing 7, sends on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49. Customer-Success: first at day 7, maximum 2, spacing 14, sends on days 7 and 21. Internal-Approval: first reminder 1 business day, maximum 3 reminders, spacing 1 business day - and THE EXISTING APPROVAL SLA IS THE HARD DEADLINE. SLA expiry always takes precedence over the reminder count. GLOBAL: Monday-Friday business week; 10:00-19:00 sending window; contact timezone when known and agency timezone as fallback; a message due outside the window moves to the next eligible business sending time; consent required for client and lead automated communication; NO CONSENT = NO SEND; stop conditions as defined; owner override always available; idempotency required. EXECUTION CONTRACT, ten steps in order: trigger satisfied, rhythm active, required channel consent exists, contact not opted out or suppressed, stop conditions false, state unchanged in any way that cancels the sequence, business-hours and timezone rules satisfied, idempotency prevents duplicates, the message goes through the central outbound chokepoint, and both the decision and the resulting send are audited. AI agents must not bypass consent, suppression, stop conditions or escalation. CORRECTION HISTORY, recorded because the first values contradicted themselves and were not silently repaired: Sales-Active and Sales-Nurture were first given as maximum 3 attempts while listing only two sends each, against the convention Customer-Success set where Day 0 is the trigger. The owner resolved it upward to 7 for both, listing every send day explicitly. Calendar-versus-business days and the Internal-Approval/SLA interaction were the other two ambiguities, both resolved in the same correction. CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING, not an objection: under Sales-Active a client who never replies receives SEVEN automated messages over twenty business days, and ADM-11 means no human reads any of them first. That volume is the owner's deliberate choice, raised from three, and is recorded so it is visible rather than discovered.

adminDecisions.question: What consent/communication policy must apply before AgencyOS sends automated outbound messages?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED for the policy. Automated client and lead follow-ups require RECORDED communication consent before AgencyOS may send them automatically, and the model must be CHANNEL-SPECIFIC: WhatsApp consent is not email consent is not SMS consent, and consent for one channel must never be assumed for another. The consent record must support contact/lead, channel, status, source/method, timestamp, withdrawal timestamp where applicable, and audit history. RULE: if required consent is absent, DO NOT SEND. If consent is withdrawn, STOP future automated follow-ups for that channel. SUPPRESSION MUST BE ENFORCED BY THE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM, NOT MERELY BY THE UI. ADMIN: must be able to see the communication-permission state. Any exceptional or manual override must require an authorized role, be explicit, be auditable, and record who, when and why. AI AGENTS: must not grant themselves communication consent and must not bypass suppression or opt-out rules. ADM-11 remains valid - once a follow-up is authorised by the communication policy, the AI-generated message may be sent without human pre-review. SCOPE: this decision does NOT define follow-up timing; ADM-69 remains separate and unanswered. REQUIRES CLARIFICATION, on the owner's explicit instruction rather than invented: the transactional-versus-sales distinction. The owner directs that transactional and service communication be separated from sales and marketing follow-up WHERE THE EXISTING BUSINESS RULES REQUIRE IT. Searched docs/business-os and docs: the words transactional, marketing and promotional appear NOWHERE in any AgencyOS document. No existing rule makes the distinction, so there is nothing to apply and the policy for transactional messages is unspecified. Recorded as owed rather than guessed.
adminDecisions.requiresClarification: the transactional-versus-sales distinction. No AgencyOS document uses the words transactional, marketing or promotional, so no existing rule requires the separation and none can be applied without inventing one.

adminDecisions.question: May a client still DECLINE a quotation that has lapsed?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 by the consumer review ADM-71 requirement 7 demanded. record_proposal_response guards on `if v_row.status <> 'sent'` BEFORE it reaches the validity check, so the moment a row moves to lapsed the function returns not_sent for BOTH responses. Today a lapsed quote can still be refused - deliberately, and the migration comment says so: 'A quote whose date has passed cannot be accepted - that is what a validity period is - but it can still be refused.' Option A removes that silently unless the implementation is told to preserve it. Requirement 6 preserves the acceptance rejection and says nothing about the refusal path. Not to be invented.
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED (delegated 2026-08-14 under the owner standing authorization): YES. record_proposal_response already accepted a refusal after the validity date and refused only acceptance, deliberately - that is what a validity period IS. It bounds what a client may say yes to, not whether they may say no. Persisting the lapse would have removed that SILENTLY, because the not_sent guard ran before the validity check: the moment the row read lapsed, a decline came back not_sent. The principle the owner set - never silently remove a client legitimate ability to decline - decides this on its own.

adminDecisions.question: Is lapsed terminal, or may a lapsed quotation be superseded, extended or revived?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 by the same review. PROPOSAL_TRANSITIONS currently lets every live state be superseded and makes accepted, rejected and superseded terminal. Nothing states which of those lapsed is. Three sub-questions, none answered anywhere: may drafting a new version supersede a lapsed one, or does the lapsed row simply stay lapsed while the new version becomes live - which would give 'replaced' two different terminal states; may an owner extend a validity date and return the quote to sent; and may a lapsed quote be revived at all. Requirement 5 preserves history and does not say which state history keeps.
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED (delegated 2026-08-14): TERMINAL, with exactly two exits - lapsed to rejected (ADM-77) and lapsed to superseded. NOT extendable and NOT revivable. Both would mean editing a validity date that has already passed, and a date that moves was never a commitment: the record would then disagree with what the client was actually told, which the owner principles forbid twice over (never lie about historical state, never fabricate dates). To re-offer, draft the next version - that already works, leaves the original intact as evidence, and is auditable, where reviving would overwrite the only record of what expired. Smallest coherent state machine.

adminDecisions.question: Does anyone get told when a quotation lapses, and who?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 by the same review. ADM-71 requirement 8 names notifications and client messaging as behaviour not to be invented. Nothing anywhere says whether a lapse notifies the owner, the assigned staff, the client, or nobody. The expiry job will emit an event because that is how this system works; whether anything subscribes to it, and what it says to whom, is unspecified. G-096's approval expiry is a precedent for the mechanism and answers nothing about the audience.
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED (delegated 2026-08-14): NOBODY automatically, and no notification machinery is added. Telling a client their offer expired is a SALES ACTION A HUMAN TAKES, carrying a judgement about whether to re-offer, discount or let it go. An automated message would also be client-facing communication, and the consent policy governing that is ADM-81 - still open - so building a sender now would either pre-empt that decision or quietly widen it. Internally nothing needs sending: the status change IS the signal, because LIVE_PROPOSAL_STATUSES stops counting the row and a queue of outstanding quotations stops showing it, which is the whole complaint G-111 was raised about. proposal.lapsed is emitted for audit and observability and has no client-facing consumer.

adminDecisions.question: Approve the proposed Admin-configurable onboarding baseline for G-113, or ask for a different shape?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 because ADM-73 granted the principle and explicitly withheld implementation: 'Do not implement until the proposed model is reviewed.' This records that the approval is owed rather than leaving G-113 waiting on nothing anybody can see. It is a design approval, not a business rule - the business rule is ADM-73 and it is granted. THE PROPOSAL, for review and not built: move seed_onboarding's 17 items out of the function's literal VALUES list into org-scoped template rows the Admin owns, and have seed_onboarding read them. Seeding those rows with the current 17 is NOT inventing data - Document 10 section 6 specifies them by name and the code already contains them, which is precisely what distinguishes this from inventing project types. Optional second half, only if wanted: named template SETS an Admin defines and picks from at project creation, deliberately NOT keyed to any project_type enum - zero or more, by name, so a project may take the baseline, a set, or a set plus extras. That also closes the half of requirement 5 that not_applicable cannot reach: a project can opt OUT of a baseline item today and cannot opt IN to an extra one. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER: whether template sets are wanted at all or the editable baseline alone suffices; whether editing the baseline should affect existing projects or only future ones; and whether an Admin may delete a baseline item or only deactivate it, since a deleted item silently changes what 'complete' meant for projects already onboarded.
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED (delegated 2026-08-14 under the owner standing authorization). The proposed shape is approved in its SMALLEST form, because inspection showed the gap was narrower than its title: THREE of the five things a template system usually needs already worked. An item could already be marked not_applicable (the status CHECK has admitted it since the table was created); an extra item could already be added to one project (onboarding_items_write admits core.can_manage_delivery, so a delivery manager can insert any key and label); and items already carry a free-form key and label rather than an enum. ONLY THE DEFAULT LIST was unreachable - seventeen values rows inside projects.seed_onboarding, changeable only by migration. So the answer is one table, one substitution and a backfill, NOT a template engine. NO PROJECT TYPE AND NO SERVICE CATEGORIES: ADM-73 established project type is the wrong axis and nothing here reintroduces it - one baseline per organization, edited directly. THE ONE GENUINE SUB-CHOICE, decided conservatively: a baseline change affects FUTURE projects only and never rewrites a project that already has a checklist. That list is a record of what the project was asked to do; editing the baseline must not make a delivered project retroactively incomplete, nor erase evidence that somebody did the work. It is also the reversible direction - an explicit apply-to-existing action can be added later as a deliberate act, whereas silently rewriting history cannot be undone. AN EMPTY BASELINE IS ALLOWED, because business rule 02 section 3.3 says onboarding blocks nothing and every item is a reminder; falling back to a built-in list would be the hidden behaviour this gap exists to remove.

adminDecisions.question: What consent policy governs transactional and service communication, as distinct from sales and marketing follow-up?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14. ADM-70 granted the consent policy and directed that transactional and service communication be separated from sales and marketing follow-up WHERE EXISTING BUSINESS RULES REQUIRE IT - and the words transactional, marketing and promotional appear nowhere in any AgencyOS document, so no existing rule requires anything and none can be applied without inventing one. ADM-69 then deferred situation 6, pending payment, on exactly this ground. This id records the owed clarification so the deferral is visible rather than implicit. It blocks ONLY the payment follow-up portion of G-012; situations 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are fully decided by ADM-69 and ADM-70. The concrete question it must answer: may AgencyOS chase an unpaid invoice without recorded marketing consent, on the ground that a payment reminder concerns an existing obligation rather than a sale - and if so, what consent or suppression still applies to it.
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED (delegated 2026-08-14 under the owner standing authorization): THERE IS NO TRANSACTIONAL EXCEPTION. Every client-facing send requires recorded consent on the channel. ADM-70 recorded the finding that decides this: the words transactional, marketing and promotional appear NOWHERE in any AgencyOS document, so there is no existing rule to apply and nothing to separate without inventing it. A transactional category is also the exact shape a broad marketing exception takes on its way in - every message anybody wants to send can be argued to service an existing relationship, and drawing that line requires a business judgement nobody has made. If the owner later wants a carve-out, adding one to this model is a smaller and more reviewable change than removing one that was assumed. What this does NOT block: a human messaging a client from their own phone. It governs what AgencyOS sends. INTERNAL-AUDIENCE messages are outside consent entirely, keyed off conversation kind rather than off the caller - the trap ADM-70 named, because the approval announcement runs through the same chokepoint and suppressing it would silently break G-110.

adminDecisions.title: The agent roster, and the order it is built in
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED. Target roster of THIRTEEN agents, built in three layers, each layer passing its architecture and verification gates before the next is activated. FOUNDATION (layer 1): requirement_collector, orchestrator, developer, qa. The minimum that proves requirements -> orchestration -> implementation -> independent verification. CORE (layer 2): sales, project_manager, ui_designer, ui_prototype, handover. OPERATIONS (layer 3): finance, support, customer_success, upsell. NOT APPROVED as separate agents: lead_qualifier, proposal_drafter, security_reviewer, estimator. Their capabilities live inside approved agents. SALES is one agent, not three. Lead qualification, requirement collection where appropriate, proposal drafting, follow-up, objection handling and negotiation support belong inside it, kept MODULAR INTERNALLY so they can be split later if scale justifies it. lead_qualifier and proposal_drafter are not activated as runtime agents. ORCHESTRATOR vs PROJECT_MANAGER is a mandatory distinction: the orchestrator is system-level - routing, context assembly, handoffs, workflow coordination. The project manager is project-level - planning, decomposition, assignment, dependencies, monitoring, blockers, coordination, initiating QA, escalation. THE ORCHESTRATOR MUST NOT judge completion, act as QA, override QA, or certify delivery. QA is the independent verifier and no other agent may declare another agent's work complete. DELIVERY stays three agents because the documented project lifecycle separates design -> prototype -> build, and deliverables.kind carries exactly those. All client review continues through the approval engine. HANDOVER is accepted as a separate future agent because it is an explicit lifecycle stage - delivery -> handover -> completed -> maintenance - and it must not be the same authority that produced what it certifies. It consumes QA evidence, production-readiness evidence, approved deliverables, client approval, deployment state and handover-package state, and must never expose secrets. SECURITY_REVIEWER is NOT created now: security verification folds into QA, which must have explicit capabilities for RLS, tenant isolation, authorization, approval bypass, secrets, prompt injection, cross-project context isolation and agent tool authorization. A specialist may be introduced later and must not be created silently. SUPPORT, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS and UPSELL stay three, as different lifecycle responsibilities. UPSELL HAS ZERO PRICING AUTHORITY: it may identify and recommend internally and must never invent a price, calculate a quote, offer a discount, negotiate price or make a commercial commitment. Pricing remains human-owned under ADM-22. ESTIMATOR is REJECTED as proposed. It must not own pricing, discounts, quotations or commercial commitments. A later 'effort_estimator' limited to engineering effort, complexity, sizing, sequencing and approximate workload - never money - would be a NEW decision. PROPOSAL_DRAFTER: the seeded description claims it drafts 'scope, timeline, and pricing'. The pricing portion contradicts an absolute rule and approval cannot make it permissible. To be corrected as part of G-125; historical records are not to be deleted. AUTHORITY INVARIANTS preserved: L2 is never granted merely because an agent needs it; agents cannot settle approvals or bypass the approval engine; agents cannot invent pricing, discounts or commercial commitments; client-facing communication requires consent; WhatsApp replies stay advisory unless a future authenticated mechanism is explicitly approved; QA is independent of the producer; the orchestrator cannot certify completion; agents cannot self-certify consequential work without independent evidence; prompt injection must never create authority; provider keys are never exposed to agents as unrestricted secrets; cross-tenant and cross-project context isolation is mandatory. RAISED BY THE GATE, and recorded because the roster was made consistent with them rather than around them: the seeded proposal_drafter contradicts business rules 08 section 5.1 today, and the earlier upsell proposal wrongly carried 'price via approval' when ADM-22 permits no agent pricing at any level.

adminDecisions.question: Approve the Agent Foundation Specification, or ask for a different shape?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED with four answers and two corrections. (1) ai.agents gains definition_version, disabled_reason and last_validated_at, with constraints so that definition_version cannot claim validation when the definition is absent, disabled_reason is REQUIRED when enabled is false and ABSENT when enabled is true, and last_validated_at cannot imply validation of a missing definition. Not over-designed: the registry remains authoritative for capability and authority; ai.agents is deployment state. (2) ONE shared ai.handoffs table, because the correlation model is shared across layers and one table makes cross-layer tracing possible without duplicating schema. Structural constraints kept - from_agent <> to_agent, and completed requires verification - PLUS a new one the owner added: the receiving agent must be an allowed handoff target in the SENDER's registry definition. (3) QA rejection does NOT require approval. It is an internal verification verdict, not a consequential business action: the producer receives the rejection and its reasons, work returns to them, retry or rework may occur, and exhaustion escalates. QA cannot approve its own rejection, and no other agent may override a verification verdict merely to make a workflow appear complete. A consequential action CAUSED by a rejection follows the normal approval rules independently. (4) Agent runs do NOT go in audit.audit_log. agent_runs and agent_steps are observability - what the agent DID. audit.audit_log is business-state change - what CHANGED - and agent-generated writes are already captured by the row-change trigger. Execution telemetry would flood a log that is narrow on purpose. CORRECTION 11, to the document rather than to the decision: the autonomy table said 'anything reaching a client = L2 = consent gate AND approval', which is too broad and would have turned ADM-70 and ADM-11 into a universal human-review gate. ADM-11 explicitly permits certain automated client follow-ups WITHOUT human review. The distinction is now: CLIENT COMMUNICATION is consent-gated and subject to the applicable communication policy; CONSEQUENTIAL CLIENT ACTION is approval-gated where existing business rules require approval. Internal approval announcements remain outside the client-communication consent gate, as ADM-74 and ADM-70 already established. CORRECTION 12, to the tool table: 'crm.sendMessage = L2 + consent + approval' is too broad if read as every invocation needing a human approval. The tool must enforce the policy applicable to the particular message - audience, consent, purpose, whether it is consequential, whether ADM-11 permits autonomous sending, and whether an approval is otherwise required. THE MODEL MUST NEVER DECIDE WHICH POLICY APPLIES; the policy layer determines it.

adminDecisions.question: Approve the Multi-Model Routing design, or ask for a different shape?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED with five answers. (5) SECOND PROVIDER DEFERRED. OpenAI is not to be chosen merely because ARCHITECTURE section 6.4 mentions it for embeddings - generation and embeddings are different capabilities. ADM-84 defines the abstraction and routing model WITHOUT committing to a second generation provider; the adapter becomes a separate implementation decision once a provider is selected. (6) ai.models is PER-ORGANIZATION, because AgencyOS is tenant-scoped throughout and one organization's model deprecation must not alter another's behaviour. A global catalog, if ever needed, is introduced deliberately rather than by making the first implementation global. (7) optimise_for is PER CATEGORY - engineering, coordination, client-facing, extraction, design, money, certification - which gives Admin control without thirteen independent tuning knobs. An agent may express a model preference; it must never become a hard dependency. (8) QA REJECTION RATE IS NOT FED INTO ROUTING AUTOMATICALLY. It is reported to the Admin and made observable. An autonomous feedback loop that changes model selection because another agent rejected work is a second-order control loop introduced before the routing system has evidence of stability. First measure, then decide. Automatic adaptation would be a separate decision. (9) THE KEY VAULT WAITS FOR ADM-60, confirmed. The encryption key is itself a production credential and its custodian is one of ADM-60's five deferred facts. The routing half proceeds independently. ROUTING INVARIANTS, mandatory: agents declare capabilities and never vendor identity; the model registry determines capability compatibility; routing policy determines preference and order; availability filters candidates; an explicit Admin override wins; resolveProvider(modelId) remains the provider boundary; fallback records the reason AND the model actually used, with no silent fallback; no agent receives provider credentials; credentials never enter prompts, agent context, database rows or ordinary logs; cost ceilings and max steps remain enforced; and routing cannot increase an agent's authority, bypass RLS, bypass approval, create money authority, or create client-send authority.

adminDecisions.question: Which second generation provider, and on whose account?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 with E1. ADM-84 DEFERRED this deliberately and said the second-provider adapter becomes a separate implementation decision once a provider is selected - explicitly NOT OpenAI merely because ARCHITECTURE section 6.4 names it for embeddings, because generation and embeddings are different capabilities. This is a business and external decision rather than an engineering one: it carries an account, a billing relationship, and credentials whose custodian is one of ADM-60's five deferred facts. Nothing here is to be chosen to make the architecture look finished. WHAT IT BLOCKS: G-129 only - real models cannot be recorded until a provider exists to serve them. The routing tables, capability matching, policy and fallback all proceed without it. WHAT IT DOES NOT BLOCK, and this is worth stating: nothing in the foundation, nothing in the existing Anthropic path, and no agent work. THE HONEST LIMIT UNTIL IT IS ANSWERED: the provider abstraction remains ASSERTED RATHER THAN DEMONSTRATED. resolveProvider has never had two adapters to choose between, so the property that callers name a model and never a vendor is a design claim that no run has ever exercised.

adminDecisions.title: Is membership of a project group itself a basis for AgencyOS to message it?
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED 2026-08-17 = A (membership is the basis): a project group is messaged on group membership, and per-contact consent is required only for direct conversations. This was already the behaviour - crm.send_outbound_message runs the per-contact consent check for kind=direct only, and a project_group falls through by design - so there is no code change; the decision is recorded and pinned live by verify-consent section 6 (a project_group send succeeds with no consent row). The accepted limitation stands: a withdrawn contact who remains in the WhatsApp group still receives group messages, because AgencyOS does not control group membership. RAISED 2026-08-14 as a precise gate rather than decided, because it is a genuine business judgement. WHAT THE REPOSITORY ESTABLISHES: business rule 02 section 5.1 defines the project group as client + agency and as THE CLIENT-FACING THREAD FOR ONE PROJECT, so a message there reaches the client. ADM-70 and ADM-81 make consent PER CONTACT PER CHANNEL, and no client-facing send happens without a recorded granted row. A crm.conversations row of kind project_group carries NO contact_id. WHAT THE REPOSITORY DOES NOT ANSWER: whether being in the group is itself the permission. Section 5.1 says what the group is FOR, never whether AgencyOS may message it absent consent. THREE IMPLEMENTABLE OPTIONS, and crm.contacts.client_account_id makes all three reachable. (A) MEMBERSHIP IS THE BASIS: the group exists because the client engaged, so no per-contact consent is required. Simplest, closest to section 5.1 framing, and it creates one channel where consent does not apply - a contact who withdrew still receives messages there. (B) AT LEAST ONE granted consent among the client account contacts. Something recorded gates it, but a withdrawn contact still sees anything sent to the group. (C) EVERY contact in the account must have granted. Strictest, and one withdrawal silences the project group entirely, which may stop delivery communication for a project the client is paying for. THE LIMITATION THAT SHOULD INFORM THE CHOICE: consent withdrawal CANNOT BE HONOURED INSIDE A GROUP by any of the three. WhatsApp group membership is controlled by the group, not by AgencyOS, so a contact who withdraws but stays in the group keeps receiving messages whatever this decides. Only removing them from the group stops that, and AgencyOS does not control who is in a group. Option C is therefore stricter in the record than in effect. CURRENT BEHAVIOUR PENDING THIS DECISION: project groups are gated by NO consent record - effectively option A - because the alternative refused every group send and broke the group messaging G-014 and G-109 deliberately built. That is recorded rather than hidden, and it is narrow: project groups only, never direct client messaging, never the internal group.

adminDecisions.title: May historical-lead reactivation run automatically, and on whom?
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED 2026-08-17 under the owner's sales-reactivation mandate. The inactive_lead follow-up situation (ADM-69 ordinal 7) would nurture every open lead. DECISION: reactivation is OPT-IN, not a default. An organization-level gate (core.organizations.reactivation_pilot_enabled) ships OFF; even ON, only leads explicitly enrolled in the cohort (crm.leads.in_reactivation_pilot) are reached, and a lead may be enrolled only if its contact holds a granted whatsapp consent row - consent is never inferred from historical WhatsApp presence. Enable/disable and enrolment are audited; both flags are writable only through the sanctioned SECURITY DEFINER functions (owner/ops_admin, tenant-scoped), and a direct Data-API PATCH by an authenticated caller, even an owner, is refused by a guard trigger. Per-tick batching and rhythm spacing are unchanged, so no thundering herd. CONSEQUENCE ACCEPTED: while the gate is off, inactive_lead nurture does not run for fresh cold leads either, not only historical ones - reactivation of any kind is opt-in per org. Import, prioritization and pilot activation are kept as separate stages; nothing sends until Meta/WABA, an AI provider, the timezone and real consent evidence are separately verified.

adminDecisions.title: How does a post-project follow-up reach a client whose leads are gone?
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED 2026-08-17. ADM-69 situation 8 (post-project) had no conversation kind to send on: direct needs a lead, and a completed project's client account outlives its leads; project_group is G-136; internal_group is not a client. DECISION: add a fourth conversation kind, client_account, keyed to the client account rather than a lead, carrying the account's contact - one thread per account (the relationship channel outlives individual projects). The worker resolves-or-creates it for post-project and sends on it. Consent is NOT a new rule: a client_account thread has an identifiable contact, so the existing per-contact-per-channel consent chokepoint gates it exactly as for direct - it is client-facing communication. The alternative (reusing the lost lead's old direct thread) was rejected: it resurrects a conversation the lifecycle considers finished.

adminDecisions.title: Do ADM-69 situations 2 and 3 fire their own follow-up, or collapse into situation 1?
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED 2026-08-17. ADM-69 situations 2 (no response after requirements request) and 3 (no response after proposal) have no observable fact separating them from situation 1: in this schema sales.proposals IS the quotation, so all three would key on the same sent_at, and firing all three would chase one client three times for one silence - exactly the duplicate ADM-69's idempotency requirement exists to prevent. DECISION: collapse 2 and 3 into situation 1 (no_response_after_quotation). The observer (crm.observe_follow_up_candidates) already never offered them; this marks them non-runnable in the situation registry (blockedBy set) so the code stops claiming they run, and escalationFor returns null for them. No new schema and no new send path; if a distinguishing fact is ever recorded, they can be un-collapsed deliberately.

adminDecisions.title: How is reactivation priority decided - a score, or recorded facts?
adminDecisions.rationale: GRANTED 2026-08-17 under the owner's sales-reactivation mandate. DECISION: no numeric lead score and no invented weights - the repository has no approved scoring model and inventing one is out of scope. Priority is a deterministic fact-tier order over eligible leads: previously_quoted > previously_replied > has_conversation > cold; within a tier, most-recently-active first, with phone then lead id as a stable tie-break. Prioritisation runs AFTER deduplication (an import-time concern) and consent-eligibility filtering: only leads whose contact holds a granted whatsapp consent row are ranked, so an unknown/no-consent lead never appears and cannot enter an outbound queue by ranking highly.

adminDecisions.title: The sales agent answers an inbound WhatsApp message itself
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-22 - GRANTED, in the owner's own words: "ai agent khud kare". WIDENS ADM-11. Until now ADM-61 section 4 recorded follow-ups as "the only path in AgencyOS where something reaches a client unread", and ADM-61 section 3 required anything else client-facing to go to the internal group. A conversational reply to an inbound WhatsApp message is now the SECOND such path: the sales agent composes and sends it, and nobody reads it first. RAISED BEFORE IT WAS GRANTED: Doc 03 section 5 ("Respond to new WhatsApp leads") and Doc 08 section 6 (AGENT -> RESPONSE -> SEND) both ask for this, and ADM-61 forbade it; the conflict was reported with three options - agent drafts and a person sends, agent drafts and the internal group approves, or ADM-11 is widened - and the owner chose the third. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the five absolutes of ADM-61 section 5 still hold at every level. The reply may not invent a price or a discount (ADM-22), promise a delivery date it was not given, claim work that does not exist, write a client credential, or treat a client's word as a fact. Those are enforced in the schema and at the row, not in the prompt. Consent (ADM-70) still gates every send through crm.send_outbound_message, and the agent still may not grant it. SCOPE: this decision is about replying inside a conversation the CLIENT started. It says nothing about agent-initiated outbound beyond the ADM-69 follow-ups, and nothing about any other agent.

adminDecisions.title: A person who messages us first has consented to be answered on that thread
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-22 - taken as the necessary consequence of ADM-91 and STATED BACK TO THE OWNER BEFORE IT WAS ACTED ON, because ADM-70 says an AI agent must not grant consent and whether an inbound message constitutes consent appears NOWHERE in any of the 23 documents. THE RULE: when a contact sends AgencyOS a WhatsApp message, crm.ingest_whatsapp_message records communication_consent for that contact on that channel with source "inbound_message" and the message as evidence. Without it every reply - agent or human - is refused with no_consent, so ADM-91 could not take effect at all. WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not consent to be added to a campaign, and it is not consent for any other channel. ADM-70 is unchanged in every other respect - the record is per contact per channel, withdrawal still stops sending, suppression is still enforced by crm.send_outbound_message rather than by any UI, and the row carries who or what recorded it so an operator can see that the system inferred it rather than a person entering it. REVERSIBLE: withdrawing consent for a contact stops replies to them immediately, and the withdrawal is refused deletion (20260815130000) so it cannot be erased and re-granted.

adminDecisions.title: An image a client sends is read by the model, described in words, and never stored
adminDecisions.why: OWNER INSTRUCTION 2026-08-22, brief section 28: "If the customer sends an image: if vision capability is available: analyze it... Do not say 'Not transcribed' if the system actually has the capability to inspect the image. If image understanding is unavailable: do not pretend." Section 29 adds that the words in an image may be Hindi, Hinglish or mixed and must not be assumed English. WHY THIS IS NOT THE VOICE-NOTE DECISION: migration 20260821120000 deferred transcription because it needed a speech provider, a decision about which, and a rule for what an uncertain transcript may be used for. None of that applies to an image - ARCHITECTURE.md 6.4 already names Anthropic, the model in ai.agents.default_model already accepts images, and no second vendor, key or bill appears. Audio remains deferred. THE SHAPE CHOSEN, and it is a choice: the image is read ONCE, into a description stored beside the message, rather than re-sent to the model on every turn. That gives every existing consumer - the reply, the intent read, the qualification read, the requirement collector - the content for free with no second system, bounds the cost, and makes the reading auditable as a row a human can read. The trade, stated rather than hidden: the sales agent reads a description and not the picture, so a judgement needing the pixels is not available to it. WHAT IS NOT STORED: the image. It is fetched into memory, read, and dropped - no bucket, no retention window, no second access-control surface, and no copy of a client's photograph in this system. Section 27 ("never expose one customer's information to another customer") is then a property of the description's tenancy rather than a policy somebody must remember to write, and a description is additionally redacted of any run of twelve or more digits before it is written, in code rather than in the schema so that a payment screenshot cannot be the one message that fails validation and goes unanswered.

adminDecisions.question: Which speech-to-text service, on whose account - and is OpenAI acceptable for it?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-23 with G-143, and raised rather than assumed BECAUSE ADM-84 section 5 already refused the reasoning that would have made it easy: OpenAI is not to be chosen merely because ARCHITECTURE section 6.4 names it for embeddings, since generation and embeddings are different capabilities. Transcription is a THIRD capability and the same rule applies to it. ADM-85 records what makes this a business question rather than an engineering one - an account, a billing relationship, and credentials whose custodian is one of ADM-60's five deferred facts. WHAT WAS BUILT ANYWAY, and why that is not the decision being taken for the owner: the capability is a port (AiTranscriber), deliberately separate from AiProvider so that no vendor named for generation can be mistaken for a candidate; the first adapter is one file and one line in router.ts, so a different vendor is a cheap change rather than a rewrite. The adapter written is OpenAI's, chosen on a CAPABILITY argument rather than familiarity - these recordings are Hindi/English code-switching, which is the case general speech APIs handle worst - and that argument is the owner's to accept or reject. WHAT IT BLOCKS: nothing that was working before. Without OPENAI_API_KEY there is no transcriber, a voice note is recorded and not heard, the transcript says so, and the client is still answered. THE EXTERNAL ACTION REQUIRED: an OpenAI account and OPENAI_API_KEY set in the deployment. Nothing here fabricates it.

adminDecisions.title: While the WABA lacks Groups eligibility, the internal announcement channel is a person's own WhatsApp, one to one
adminDecisions.why: GRANTED BY THE ADMIN 2026-08-23, in their own words: 'ha bana do 1:1 wala'. The context that forced the decision: G-109 built the internal channel as a WhatsApp GROUP, and on the first real WABA this system has ever had, Meta answered what no documentation could - error #131215, 'This phone number is not eligible to access Groups APIs', established by the Admin running the Graph calls themselves (GET /{pnid}/groups answered an empty list; POST answered 131215). A Cloud API number cannot join a group made in the ordinary app either, so the group channel cannot deliver on this deployment with any id and any UI. WHAT THE GRANT PERMITS: a conversation kind internal_direct - the owner's own number, linked from /settings (organization.settings, the owner alone), addressed as an individual, consent-exempt exactly as the internal group is because ADM-70 governs clients and this is the agency talking to itself. Announcements that went to the group go to the person: the approval with the full quotation and its PDF (G-155/G-156), the escalation with its reason (G-146 era). WHAT THE GRANT DOES NOT MOVE: ADM-74 stands whole - the WhatsApp message remains advisory, no reply settles anything, the approval is decided only in AgencyOS. PREFERENCE, decided here: while both a group and a person are linked, the PERSON wins - on this deployment a linked group is a row Meta will refuse to deliver to, and an announcement that reaches a person outranks one that reaches a constraint. The preference lives in one function (internalChannel in crm/handlers.ts) and flipping it the day Meta grants Groups eligibility is a one-line decision. Gap G-159 implements this.

adminDecisions.title: The agent does everything but decide: it prices the draft, submits it, sends what the owner approves, and redrafts from the owner's note
adminDecisions.why: GRANTED BY THE ADMIN 2026-08-23, in their own words: 'agent sab kuch kre mai bs pdf approve changes karo' - the agent does everything; the owner's two verbs are approve and changes, exercised against the quotation PDF on their phone and settled in AgencyOS. WHAT THIS REVISES, precisely: ADM-22's letter said 'it must never state a price'. Revised: the agent may PROPOSE a price on an internal draft, grounded in the agency's own 45-quotation corpus (the 2026-08-23 Quotation Intelligence study: floor 25,000, modal complete-system 50,000, the five observed levers), and no price reaches a client until a person has decided it - the human act moved from typing the number to approving it. The same grant retires sales.refuse_priced_by_nobody (its rule no longer exists to hold), exempts the two internal channel kinds from crm.refuse_unread_price (the price announced to the owner is how the number acquires its human - suppressing it handed the owner a question with the question removed), lets the scope job OPEN the deal it quotes against (G-088's one-open-deal index enforces the shape; a deal row is internal bookkeeping under ADM-61 section 2), and makes the decision itself an event (approval.decided) so approval SENDS the approved quotation to the client authored with the decider, and changes_requested hands the note to the agent for the next version. WHAT THIS DOES NOT MOVE, stated as firmly as what it does: ADM-07 whole - the owner approves before anything is sent, and the approval engine is now the ONLY human gate, which is why nothing in this grant weakens it; ADM-74 whole - the WhatsApp message remains advisory, no reply settles anything, the decision happens in AgencyOS authenticated; ADM-22's client-facing core whole - an agency message stating a price to a CLIENT still requires a named human author, and the dispatch satisfies it honestly by authoring with the approver; the five absolutes of 08-ai-agent-responsibilities section 5, with absolute 1 reworded to what it always protected: an agent must never state a price to a client that no human has decided. Discounts, payment terms, taxes and dates remain entirely the owner's - the schema has no field for them. Recording a client's acceptance also stays a person's act (absolute 5: a client's word is a claim, not a fact). G-162 implements this.

adminDecisions.question: What is a 3-plan quotation in the engine - three sibling proposals, plans inside the document, or a plan-set above proposals?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-24 with G-166, deferred deliberately from G-165 rather than smuggled into a jsonb blob. The Master Quotation System's Part H says WHEN plans are warranted; the engine models ONE proposal = one price and everything downstream assumes it (one approval amount, one money-floor resolution, one dispatched total, one recorded answer). Three candidate models, each with a real cost, recorded on G-166: (a) sibling proposals sharing a requirement version - closest to existing machinery, but proposals_live_version_key allows one live version and 'sent' would mean three live documents; (b) plans inside proposals.document with the total being the recommended plan's - the arithmetic goes murky the moment the client picks another tier; (c) a plan-set table above proposals whose client choice mints the real proposal - cleanest semantics, most new surface. The owner's call, because each option changes what 'the owner approved' MEANS for a multi-plan offer - and that is ADM-96's own hinge.
